rulings.reason: The instruction tells the judge to score a structural dependency property (presence of a URL or image payload, count of stray hashtags, tag clutter) rather than the wit itself, and it explicitly says to score the dependency and not the topic, so a completely unfunny but self-contained single-tag line earns a 10 and a high score carries no evidence about how good the entry is. Its signal runs only in the low direction as a surface format fingerprint of how the item was posted, which is exactly a Track-B nuisance, though it is mixed because the discipline of landing a joke in visible words alone plausibly co-produces genuine craft.
